items.title: Structure of the normalization of a locally Noetherian scheme of dimension one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma collects six properties of the normalization morphism of a locally Noetherian scheme of dimension one: integrality, surjectivity and bijectivity on components; factorization through the reduction; birationality; the identification of the stalks of the pushforward with integral closures; finiteness of the fibres and of the residue field extensions; and the local description as a finite product of Dedekind domains. The proof observes that most of these are general properties of the normalization but singles out exactly what is not automatic - finiteness of the fibres, finiteness of the residue field extensions and the local Dedekind structure - and reduces those to the affine Noetherian reduced one-dimensional case, then to a one-dimensional Noetherian domain, where the properties follow from Krull-Akizuki (proof lines 8794-8811). H2: the identification of which parts are not covered by general theory and the reduction to the Dedekind case are the substance.
